summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Ubuntu 24.04 with Python and several development tools installed. It cleans up unnecessary files to keep the image small, then sets up an /app directory, copies in an application file, and configures the container to run that Python application when started.

explanations.4: The && chains multiple commands together so they all run as one layer; if any command fails, the whole thing stops.
explanations.15: The --break-system-packages flag allows pip to install Python packages even though Ubuntu discourages it for system Python; this is common in Docker since we control the environment.
explanations.16: apt-get clean removes cached package data that apt downloaded, which we no longer need and just wastes space.
explanations.17: This deletes temporary files and apt's package lists to further reduce the image size.
explanations.18: The find commands delete .pyc compiled Python files and __pycache__ folders which Python creates but doesn't need; 2>/dev/null silently ignores any errors.
explanations.19: The final 'true' command ensures this line succeeds even if the find commands found nothing, so the build doesn't fail.
